title: Third-Party Risk and Compliance

header.html: 5.3 Explain the assessment and management processes associated with third-party risk; 5.4 Summarize elements of effective security compliance
the official CompTIA Security+ SY0-801 V8 exam objectives, document version 2.0

html:
1Why third parties matter

Vendors, partners and cloud providers touch your data and systems, so their weaknesses become your risk (supply chain risk, module 5). Third-party risk management covers choosing, contracting, monitoring and ending the relationship.

2Vendor selection

Term Meaning
Request for information (RFI) Gather general information about what vendors offer
Request for proposal (RFP) Detailed proposal with solution and price for a defined need
Request for quote (RFQ) Price for a well-defined product or service
Expression of interest (EOI) A vendor signals interest before the formal process
Due diligence Investigating the vendor's security, finances and reputation before signing
Conflict of interest A relationship that could bias the selection

3Agreement types

Agreement Purpose
SLA (service-level agreement) Measurable service levels and penalties (uptime, response time)
SLO (service-level objective) A target inside an SLA
MOU (memorandum of understanding) Non-binding statement of shared intent
MOA (memorandum of agreement) Binding agreement on roles and actions
NDA (non-disclosure agreement) Keeps information confidential
MSA (master services agreement) Overall terms for a long-term relationship
SOW (statement of work) Specific tasks, deliverables and timeline of one project
Exam tip

. MSA = umbrella terms; SOW = one project. SLA = measurable service promise. MOU = non-binding; MOA = binding. NDA = secrecy.

4Vendor monitoring and limits

Item Meaning
Right to audit Contract clause letting you inspect the vendor
Service-level monitoring Tracking performance against the SLA
Vendor registry A list of vendors with their risk ratings
Vendor assessment Questionnaires and reviews of vendor controls
Compliance attestation A vendor's statement (often an independent report) that it meets a standard
Penetration testing Testing the vendor's systems (with permission)
Rules of engagement Written limits and permissions for a test

Limitations and constraints: staffing, resource availability, environment, legal and regulatory factors, geography and jurisdiction, financial or ROI limits, vendor lock-in, assurance mechanisms.

5Security compliance

Element Details
Compliance training Data handling, anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing (AML/CTF), anti-bribery
Compliance monitoring Attestations (formal statements) and acknowledgements (people confirm they read policies)
Consequences of non-compliance Reputational damage, financial, legal, contractual, sanctions, loss of license
Privacy Right to be forgotten, opt-in or opt-out, data correction, processing restrictions, processing prevention, controller vs processor, ownership
Legal compliance Legal hold (preserve data for litigation), legal orders, data retention requirements

Exam tip

. A legal hold overrides normal deletion: nothing relevant may be destroyed. A controller decides the purpose; a processor handles data on its behalf. Right to be forgotten = erasure on request, subject to law.

Exam tip

. A legal hold stops normal deletion of relevant data; retention requirements set how long data must be kept.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors already has a long-term contract with a supplier and now wants a document that defines one new project's tasks and deliverables. Which should it use?

  • AA master services agreement
  • BA statement of work
  • CA non-disclosure agreement
  • DA memorandum of understanding
Show the answer

Answer: B. A statement of work defines the specific tasks and deliverables, under the umbrella of the MSA.

S2A contract lets the company inspect a cloud provider's security controls on request. Which clause is this?

  • ALegal hold
  • BRight to audit
  • CRate limiting
  • DVendor lock-in
Show the answer

Answer: B. A right to audit clause allows inspection of the vendor's controls.

S3A company wants vendors to describe their offerings in general before it defines requirements. Which document fits?

  • ARFQ
  • BRFI
  • CSLA
  • DSOW
Show the answer

Answer: B. A request for information gathers general information from vendors.

S4Litigation is expected, so all emails about the project must be preserved even though the policy says to delete them after 90 days. What applies?

  • AData minimization
  • BRight to be forgotten
  • CTokenization
  • DLegal hold
Show the answer

Answer: D. A legal hold suspends normal deletion for relevant data.

S5A customer asks a company to delete the personal data it holds about them. Which privacy right is this?

  • ARight to audit
  • BProcessing prevention only
  • CData transpose
  • DRight to be forgotten
Show the answer

Answer: D. Requesting erasure of personal data is the right to be forgotten.

S6An agreement states uptime of 99.9% and credits if the vendor misses it. Which agreement is this?

  • ANDA
  • BSLA
  • CMOU
  • DEOI
Show the answer

Answer: B. A service-level agreement sets measurable service levels and remedies.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is the difference between RFI, RFP and RFQ?

Show the answer

RFI gathers information, RFP asks for a detailed proposal, RFQ asks for a price.

R2What does an MSA cover?

Show the answer

The overall terms of a long-term vendor relationship.

R3What is due diligence?

Show the answer

Investigating a vendor's security, finances and reputation before signing.

R4Name three consequences of non-compliance.

Show the answer

For example reputational damage, financial penalties, legal action, sanctions, loss of license.

R5What is a compliance attestation?

Show the answer

A formal statement, often independent, that a standard is met.

R6Controller or processor: who decides why data is processed?

Show the answer

The controller.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Selection RFI (information), RFP (proposal), RFQ (price), EOI; due diligence; conflict of interest
Agreements SLA/SLO, MOU (non-binding), MOA (binding), NDA, MSA (umbrella), SOW (project)
Monitoring right to audit, service-level monitoring, vendor registry and assessments, attestations, penetration testing, rules of engagement
Compliance training (data handling, AML/CTF, anti-bribery), attestations and acknowledgements, consequences, privacy rights, legal hold and retention
